correctness.rationale: The smallest admissible multiplier is q=2, where the selected set consists only of k=m, so the GCD is the central binomial coefficient. Kummer converts its p-adic valuation into the number of carries in m+m. The sharp maximum is r_p(m), and m has exactly r relevant digit positions; attaining r therefore means a carry exits every position. The units condition is 2d_0>=p, and induction with incoming carry 1 gives 2d_j+1>=p thereafter. The count and binary specialization follow directly. A standalone checker exhaustively verifies the finite digit equivalences over the stated test grid.

value.rationale: The question asks when an extremal invariant reaches its absolute minimum row, a natural boundary problem immediately suggested by the newly defined T_p(m). The answer is a complete structural classification rather than a numerical example: it converts the global extremal problem into an explicit base-p digit language, gives an exact count at every digit length, and identifies the full binary branch. This provides a sharp boundary complementary to the much larger p^a+1 least-row family.
